title: Unconjugated vs Conjugated Hyperbilirubinemia, Neurotoxicity and Light
summary: Sort jaundice by where bilirubin handling fails: hemolysis, Gilbert and Crigler-Najjar raise unconjugated bilirubin; Dubin-Johnson, Rotor and obstruction raise conjugated bilirubin. Learn why newborn bilirubin is judged by age in hours, gestational age and risk factors, and why bilirubin samples must be protected from light.

reviewer.note: Teaches Ch. 22 Hits 5 and 6, Exam Trap 3 and Table 2 (Quick-Compare: unconjugated vs conjugated). Checked against Huang 2022 (UGT1A1 activity and bilirubin ranges), Guerra Ruiz 2021 and Newsome 2018 (pre-hepatic, hepatic and post-hepatic patterns), Morais 2022 (Dubin-Johnson and Rotor), Bhutani 2013 and Zhang 2021 (neurotoxicity and threshold structure), and Sofronescu 2012 and Ihara 1992 (light effects; abstracts only, full texts not open access) plus Lindqvist 2025. The 2022 AAP guideline (Kemper 2022) is not open access and was not read. Two corrections: the reviewer’s Crigler-Najjar type I range (“>5, sometimes >20”) understates the typical 20–50 mg/dL (register flag rv-ch22-crigler-najjar-range); and Trap 3’s claim that light raises the direct-reacting fraction is not the general finding: light degrades bilirubin (falsely low on diazo), with method-dependent shifts between fractions (register flag rv-ch22-bilirubin-light-direction). Not taught as fact (pending): hemolysis 1.5–3.0 mg/dL, Gilbert “seldom >5”, choledocholithiasis “>90% direct, ALP frequently >300 IU/L”, and the “over 20 mg/dL” basal-ganglia figure.

objectives: Place hemolysis, Gilbert syndrome, Crigler-Najjar types 1 and 2, Dubin-Johnson, Rotor and bile-duct obstruction before or after bilirubin conjugation.
Explain why the risk of bilirubin neurotoxicity in a newborn is judged by age in hours, gestational age and risk factors rather than a single cutoff.
Predict the effect of light exposure on a bilirubin sample and state the handling rule.

scenes.title: Three yellow puzzles
scenes.altText: Invented scenario: three bilirubin requests. (1) A well young adult: total bilirubin mildly raised, mostly unconjugated; haemoglobin, reticulocytes and aminotransferases normal. (2) An adult with dark urine: bilirubin mostly direct-reacting, aminotransferases normal. (3) A 36-hour-old infant, born at 36 weeks, with rising jaundice; the tube sat uncovered under bench lights for two days before analysis. Question token: “Before or after conjugation, and can we trust the number?”

cues.text: Three bilirubin requests. A well young adult has a mildly raised, mostly unconjugated bilirubin, with normal blood count and liver enzymes.
An adult with dark urine has a mostly direct-reacting bilirubin, again with normal liver enzymes.
And a newborn’s tube sat uncovered under bench lights for two days before testing. Before or after conjugation, and can we trust the number?

props.label: Before or after conjugation? Trust the number?

scenes.title: Four stations on the bilirubin line
scenes.altText: Schematic pathway with four cards. Production: heme from senescent red cells is broken down to biliverdin and then unconjugated bilirubin, which is water-insoluble and travels bound to albumin, so it does not appear in urine. Uptake: OATP1B1 and OATP1B3 carry it into the hepatocyte. Conjugation: UGT1A1 adds glucuronic acid, giving water-soluble mono- and diglucuronides. Export: MRP2 (ABCC2) pumps conjugated bilirubin across the canalicular membrane into bile; conjugated bilirubin that reaches blood is filtered into urine.

cues.text: Bilirubin comes mainly from the breakdown of heme in old red cells. Unconjugated bilirubin does not dissolve in water, so it rides on albumin and does not pass into urine.
At the liver, the transporters OATP1B1 and OATP1B3 carry it into the hepatocyte.
There the enzyme UGT1A1 attaches glucuronic acid. The conjugated bilirubin is water-soluble.
Finally, the canalicular pump MRP2 exports it into bile. Conjugated bilirubin that leaks back into blood is filtered by the kidney, which is why it can darken urine.

scenes.title: Before or after the glucuronide
scenes.altText: Left card, unconjugated (problem before or at conjugation): hemolysis (unconjugated up, conjugated normal or slightly up; anaemia, reticulocytes; aminotransferases normal); Gilbert syndrome (UGT1A1 about 11–30% of normal activity; serum bilirubin 17–103 µmol/L, about 1–6 mg/dL; affects several percent of people; benign); Crigler-Najjar type 2 (about 10% activity; 103–342 µmol/L, about 6–20 mg/dL; responds to phenobarbital); Crigler-Najjar type 1 (no activity; 342–855 µmol/L, about 20–50 mg/dL; no phenobarbital response; risk of brain injury). Right card, conjugated (problem after conjugation): Dubin-Johnson (MRP2/ABCC2 defect; typically 2–5 mg/dL with more than half direct-reacting; black pigmented liver; normal aminotransferases); Rotor (OATP1B1 + OATP1B3 deficiency; no pigment); obstruction such as choledocholithiasis (conjugated bilirubin with raised ALP and GGT, dark urine, pale stools).

cues.text: If the problem is before or at conjugation, unconjugated bilirubin rises. In hemolysis the liver is simply overloaded: look for anaemia and raised reticulocytes, with normal liver enzymes.

Gilbert syndrome is common and harmless: UGT1A1 keeps roughly a tenth to a third of its activity, and bilirubin stays mild. In Crigler-Najjar type two, about ten percent remains and phenobarbital helps.
In Crigler-Najjar type one there is no activity at all. Bilirubin typically runs about twenty to fifty milligrams per decilitre, high enough to injure the brain.

If the problem is after conjugation, conjugated bilirubin rises and appears in urine. Dubin-Johnson is a broken MRP2 export pump with a black liver; Rotor is an uptake defect with no pigment; a common duct stone adds raised ALP and GGT.

scenes.title: The brain risk and the bench light
scenes.altText: Neurotoxicity card: unconjugated bilirubin can injure the brain, classically staining the basal ganglia (globus pallidus) and damaging auditory pathways; at the same bilirubin level, risk is higher in preterm infants. Treatment thresholds are set against postnatal age in hours, gestational age and risk factors (for example G6PD deficiency, prematurity, sepsis), not one fixed number. Light card: bilirubin is light-sensitive. In one diazo study, plasma left unprotected under artificial light at room temperature showed significant falls in total and direct bilirubin at 48 hours (delays of up to 8 hours made no significant difference), while light-protected plasma was stable for at least 24 hours; another study found that the effect of light on the bilirubin fractions depended on the method. Protect samples from light. Hook answers card.

cues.text: Severe unconjugated bilirubin can injure the brain, classically the basal ganglia and the hearing pathways. At the same level, a preterm baby is at higher risk than a term baby.
So newborn treatment thresholds are read against age in hours, gestational age and risk factors such as G6PD deficiency, never a single cutoff.

Bilirubin is also destroyed by light. In one study, plasma left uncovered under room lights read significantly lower after two days, though a few hours made no significant difference, and how light shifts the fractions depends on the method. Shield the tube.

Hook answers: the well adult fits Gilbert syndrome; the dark-urine adult has a conjugated, after-the-liver-cell pattern such as Dubin-Johnson; and the newborn needs a light-protected repeat, judged for age in hours, prematurity and risk factors.

scenes.title: Three classic traps
scenes.altText: Three trap cards: “Light on a bilirubin tube is harmless” (✓ bilirubin photodegrades: shield the sample, or results can read falsely low); “One bilirubin number defines neurotoxic risk in a newborn” (✓ thresholds depend on age in hours, gestational age and risk factors); “Crigler-Najjar type 1 runs just above 5 mg/dL” (✓ type 1 typically about 20–50 mg/dL; about 6–20 mg/dL is type 2 territory).

cues.text: Trap one: light on a bilirubin tube is harmless. No: bilirubin breaks down in light, so shield the sample or the result can read falsely low.
Trap two: one bilirubin number defines danger in a newborn. No: read it against age in hours, gestational age and risk factors.
Trap three: Crigler-Najjar type one sits just above five. No: it typically runs about twenty to fifty milligrams per decilitre; six to twenty is type two territory.

props.title: ✗ “One cutoff defines neonatal danger.”
lines: ✓ Age in hours · GA · risk factors

scenes.title: Factory, packing station, shipping door
scenes.altText: Memory aid: “The liver is a packing plant. Too many parcels arriving (hemolysis) or a slow packing station (UGT1A1: Gilbert, Crigler-Najjar) leaves UNPACKED, unconjugated bilirubin. A jammed shipping door (MRP2: Dubin-Johnson) or a blocked road (bile-duct stone) leaves PACKED, conjugated bilirubin backing up.” Tokens: too many parcels · slow packing · jammed door / blocked road. A card lists where the aid breaks.

cues.text: Memory aid: the liver is a packing plant. Too many parcels arriving, or a slow packing station, leaves unpacked, unconjugated bilirubin. A jammed shipping door or a blocked road leaves packed, conjugated bilirubin backing up.

Where it breaks: liver-cell disease can raise both fractions; Rotor syndrome is a reuptake problem, not the shipping door, yet still gives conjugated bilirubin; and a newborn can have a physiological unconjugated rise with no broken station at all.

scenes.title: Takeaway
scenes.altText: Two tokens: “Unconjugated = before or at UGT1A1 (hemolysis, Gilbert, Crigler-Najjar) · conjugated = after (Dubin-Johnson, Rotor, obstruction)”, “Newborn risk: age in hours, gestational age, risk factors · shield bilirubin samples from light”.

cues.text: Unconjugated bilirubin rises when the problem lies before or at UGT1A1 and conjugated bilirubin when it lies after, newborn levels are judged by age in hours, gestational age and risk factors, and bilirubin samples must be shielded from light.

props.label: Newborn: hours · GA · risk factors · shield from light

explanation.what: Plain language: bilirubin is a yellow waste product of old red cells. The liver takes it in, attaches glucuronic acid (a sugar acid) to make it water-soluble, and pumps it into bile. If too much arrives or the attaching step is weak, the “raw” (unconjugated) form builds up; if the pump or the bile duct fails, the processed (conjugated) form backs up and spills into urine. Scientific terms: unconjugated (indirect) and conjugated (direct-reacting) bilirubin, OATP1B1/OATP1B3, UDP-glucuronosyltransferase 1A1 (UGT1A1), MRP2 (ABCC2), Gilbert syndrome, Crigler-Najjar syndrome types 1 and 2, Dubin-Johnson syndrome, Rotor syndrome, extrahepatic cholestasis, bilirubin encephalopathy (kernicterus), photodegradation.
explanation.why: The site of failure decides which fraction rises. Unconjugated bilirubin is albumin-bound and water-insoluble, so it does not enter urine, but at high levels it can enter and injure the brain, especially in newborns. Conjugated bilirubin is water-soluble, so it is filtered into urine. Bilirubin absorbs light and is chemically changed by it, so exposed samples give wrong results.
explanation.measure: Huang 2022: UGT1A1 activity 0% in Crigler-Najjar type 1 (bilirubin 342–855 µmol/L, about 20–50 mg/dL), about 10% in type 2 (103–342 µmol/L, about 6–20 mg/dL) and about 11–30% in Gilbert syndrome (17–103 µmol/L, about 1–6 mg/dL). Gilbert syndrome affects about 3–10% (Guerra Ruiz 2021) or 5–8% (Newsome 2018) of people. Dubin-Johnson and Rotor: typically 2–5 mg/dL, more than half direct-reacting (Morais 2022). Light: in one study, unprotected plasma under artificial light showed significant falls in total and direct bilirubin at 48 hours, delays of up to 8 hours made no significant difference, and light-protected plasma was stable for at least 24 hours (Sofronescu 2012).
explanation.differs: Unconjugated (hemolysis, Gilbert, Crigler-Najjar; no bilirubin in urine) vs conjugated (Dubin-Johnson, Rotor, obstruction; bilirubinuria). Gilbert (mild, benign) vs Crigler-Najjar type 1 (no enzyme activity, very high levels, brain injury risk). Dubin-Johnson (MRP2, black liver) vs Rotor (OATP1B1 and OATP1B3, no pigment). Neonatal threshold reading (age in hours, gestational age, risk factors) vs a single cutoff.
explanation.examAngle: Expect: classify a jaundice pattern as unconjugated or conjugated and name the likely disorder; pick the disorder with a black liver; recognise that preterm or G6PD-deficient infants are treated at lower bilirubin levels; identify light exposure as a cause of a falsely low bilirubin.

comparisons.title: Unconjugated vs conjugated hyperbilirubinemia
comparisons.distinguisher: Which step fails: arrival and conjugation, or export and drainage.

mnemonic.text: The liver is a packing plant: too many parcels (hemolysis) or a slow packing station (UGT1A1: Gilbert, Crigler-Najjar) leaves UNPACKED, unconjugated bilirubin; a jammed shipping door (MRP2: Dubin-Johnson) or a blocked road (bile-duct stone) leaves PACKED, conjugated bilirubin backing up.
mnemonic.explanation: Ties the rising fraction to the step that fails.
mnemonic.limitation: Liver-cell disease can raise both fractions; Rotor syndrome is a reuptake defect, not the shipping door, yet still raises conjugated bilirubin; a newborn can have a physiological unconjugated rise with no broken station.

analogyLimitations: Bilirubin ranges come from one review and vary between patients and methods.
takeaway: Unconjugated bilirubin rises when the problem lies before or at UGT1A1 and conjugated bilirubin when it lies after, newborn levels are judged by age in hours, gestational age and risk factors, and bilirubin samples must be shielded from light.

questions.stem: A healthy 22-year-old has a total bilirubin of 2.4 mg/dL, mostly unconjugated. Haemoglobin, reticulocyte count and aminotransferases are normal. What is the most likely cause?

options.rationale: Correct. A mild, isolated unconjugated rise without hemolysis or liver injury fits reduced UGT1A1 activity in Gilbert syndrome.
Incorrect. Dubin-Johnson raises conjugated (direct-reacting) bilirubin because the MRP2 export pump fails.
Incorrect. Type 1 has no UGT1A1 activity and bilirubin typically about 20–50 mg/dL.
Incorrect. Obstruction raises conjugated bilirubin together with ALP and GGT.

questions.stem: A plasma sample for bilirubin is left uncovered under artificial room light for 48 hours before diazo analysis. What is the expected effect?

options.text: Falsely low total and direct bilirubin
options.rationale: Correct. Bilirubin photodegrades; in one study, unprotected plasma showed significant falls in total and direct bilirubin by 48 hours.

options.text: No change, because bilirubin is stable at room temperature
options.rationale: Incorrect. Stability at room temperature applied to light-protected plasma; light exposure is the problem.
Incorrect. Light destroys bilirubin, so total bilirubin falls.

options.text: A reliable result, as long as the sample is not hemolysed
options.rationale: Incorrect. Hemolysis is not the only pre-analytical problem; light exposure alone can lower the result, so the sample should be shielded.

questions.stem: A 36-hour-old infant born at 36 weeks with G6PD deficiency has a rising total serum bilirubin. How should the laboratory value be interpreted for neurotoxicity risk?

options.text: Against thresholds for the infant’s age in hours, gestational age and risk factors
options.rationale: Correct. Guidelines set treatment thresholds by postnatal age and group infants by gestational age and risk factors such as G6PD deficiency.

options.text: Against a single cutoff of 20 mg/dL for all newborns
options.rationale: Incorrect. A single number ignores age in hours, prematurity and risk factors, which lower the level at which treatment starts.
Incorrect. The neurotoxic form is unconjugated bilirubin; thresholds use total serum bilirubin.

options.text: As physiological jaundice that needs no comparison
options.rationale: Incorrect. Prematurity and G6PD deficiency are risk factors for severe hyperbilirubinemia.

references.citation: Huang MJ, Chen PL, Huang CS. Bilirubin metabolism and UDP-glucuronosyltransferase 1A1 variants in Asians: Pathogenic implications and therapeutic response. Kaohsiung J Med Sci. 2022;38(8):729-738. doi:10.1002/kjm2.12579
references.usedFor: UGT1A1 as the sole bilirubin-glucuronidating enzyme; OATP uptake and MRP2 export; UGT1A1 activity and serum bilirubin ranges for Crigler-Najjar types 1 and 2 and Gilbert syndrome; phototherapy, phenobarbital and transplant context.

references.citation: Guerra Ruiz AR, Crespo J, López Martínez RM, Iruzubieta P, Casals Mercadal G, Lalana Garcés M, Lavin B, Morales Ruiz M. Measurement and clinical usefulness of bilirubin in liver disease. Adv Lab Med. 2021;2(3):352-372. doi:10.1515/almed-2021-0047
references.usedFor: Bilirubin metabolism (albumin binding, OATP1B1/1B3, UGT1A1, ABCC2/MRP2); only conjugated bilirubin is filtered into urine; pre-hepatic (hemolysis: unconjugated up, conjugated normal or slightly up, anaemia and reticulocytes, normal aminotransferases), hepatic and post-hepatic patterns; Gilbert 3–10%; Crigler-Najjar type 1 (no phenobarbital response, kernicterus) vs type 2 (responds to phenobarbital); Dubin-Johnson pigment and normal enzymes; Rotor without pigment; choledocholithiasis with GGT/ALP rise; 1 mg/dL = 17 µmol/L.

references.citation: Newsome PN, Cramb R, Davison SM, et al. Guidelines on the management of abnormal liver blood tests. Gut. 2018;67(1):6-19. doi:10.1136/gutjnl-2017-314924
references.usedFor: Unconjugated hyperbilirubinaemia from haemolysis or impaired conjugation vs conjugated from parenchymal disease or obstruction; Gilbert syndrome as the most common cause of isolated raised bilirubin (5–8%); exclude haemolysis with reticulocytes, LDH and haptoglobin.

references.citation: Morais MB, Machado MV. Benign inheritable disorders of bilirubin metabolism manifested by conjugated hyperbilirubinemia-A narrative review. United European Gastroenterol J. 2022;10(7):745-753. doi:10.1002/ueg2.12279
references.usedFor: Dubin-Johnson (ABCC2/MRP2) and Rotor (combined OATP1B1/OATP1B3) syndromes; typical bilirubin 2–5 mg/dL, more than half direct-reacting; black liver with lysosomal pigment in Dubin-Johnson, normal histology in Rotor; normal aminotransferases; coproporphyrin patterns.

references.citation: Bhutani VK, Wong RJ. Bilirubin neurotoxicity in preterm infants: risk and prevention. J Clin Neonatol. 2013;2(2):61-69. doi:10.4103/2249-4847.116402
references.usedFor: Basal ganglia (globus pallidus) staining and auditory pathway injury; higher risk in preterm infants at the same bilirubin level; phototherapy thresholds tied to postnatal age in hours and neurotoxicity risk.

references.citation: Zhang M, Tang J, He Y, et al. Systematic review of global clinical practice guidelines for neonatal hyperbilirubinemia. BMJ Open. 2021;11(1):e040182. doi:10.1136/bmjopen-2020-040182
references.usedFor: Guidelines group infants by gestational age and risk factors for phototherapy and exchange thresholds; common risk factors (prematurity, G6PD deficiency, exclusive breastfeeding, sepsis); lower thresholds with risk factors.

references.citation: Sofronescu AG, Loebs T, Zhu Y. Effects of temperature and light on the stability of bilirubin in plasma samples. Clin Chim Acta. 2012;413(3-4):463-466. doi:10.1016/j.cca.2011.10.036
references.usedFor: Abstract only (full text not open access): light-protected plasma stable at 3 °C and 22 °C for at least 24 h; under artificial light at 22 °C, delays up to 8 h had no significant effect and total and direct bilirubin (diazo) fell significantly by 48 h, with direct falling from 5.0 to 3.5 mg/dL in elevated samples.

references.citation: Ihara H, Nakamura H, Aoki Y, Aoki T, Yoshida M. In vitro effects of light on serum bilirubin subfractions measured by high-performance liquid chromatography: comparison with four routine methods. Clin Chem. 1992;38(10):2124-2129. doi:10.1093/clinchem/38.10.2124
references.usedFor: Abstract only: light photodegrades bilirubin subfractions (unconjugated fastest, delta most stable); about 30% of photoproducts reacted as indirect bilirubin in the diazo method, while on the Ektachem method they raised the conjugated and unconjugated fractions (and lowered delta bilirubin); the effect is method-dependent; shield serum from light.

references.citation: Lindqvist D, Hansson M, Thomas M, Hulzebos CV, Vitek L, Blokzijl A, Berkel MV. Bilirubin Photoisomers in Neonatal Jaundice. Int J Mol Sci. 2025;26(21):10791. doi:10.3390/ijms262110791
references.usedFor: Bilirubin photoisomers can react in total and direct bilirubin assays to differing degrees by method (configurational isomers but not lumirubin react in the diazo method); routine methods cannot quantify photoproducts.

claims.text: Pathway: albumin-bound unconjugated bilirubin, OATP1B1/1B3 uptake, UGT1A1 conjugation, MRP2 export; only conjugated bilirubin enters urine.
Hemolysis, Gilbert and Crigler-Najjar types 1 and 2 raise unconjugated bilirubin; UGT1A1 activity and bilirubin ranges; Gilbert prevalence; phenobarbital response.
Dubin-Johnson (MRP2, black liver, 2–5 mg/dL, normal enzymes), Rotor (OATP1B1/1B3, no pigment) and obstruction (with ALP/GGT rise) raise conjugated bilirubin.
Unconjugated bilirubin neurotoxicity (basal ganglia, auditory pathways), higher preterm risk, thresholds by age in hours, gestational age and risk factors.
Light degrades bilirubin, lowering diazo total and direct results after 48 h unprotected (no significant change up to 8 h); fraction shifts are method-dependent; shield samples.
claims.note: Sofronescu and Ihara read as abstracts only.

claims.text: Reviewer figures not taught: hemolysis 1.5–3.0 mg/dL; Gilbert seldom >5 mg/dL; choledocholithiasis >90% direct with ALP frequently >300 IU/L; basal-ganglia deposition above 20 mg/dL.
claims.note: No open source read in this session gave these figures.

accuracyFlags.issue: The reviewer gives Crigler-Najjar type I as “>5, sometimes >20 mg/dL”. Huang 2022 gives 342–855 µmol/L (about 20–50 mg/dL) for type 1 and 103–342 µmol/L (about 6–20 mg/dL) for type 2, so values just above 5 mg/dL fit type 2 or Gilbert, not type 1. The lesson teaches the source ranges.

Exam Trap 3 says light photoisomerization increases the direct-reacting fraction and can “manufacture” a conjugated hyperbilirubinemia. The sources read (abstracts of Sofronescu 2012 and Ihara 1992, plus Lindqvist 2025) show that light degrades bilirubin, lowering diazo total and direct results, and that shifts between fractions depend on the method (photoproducts reacted as indirect in a diazo method but raised conjugated and unconjugated fractions on the Ektachem method). The lesson teaches “shield from light; results can read falsely low; fraction effects are method-dependent”.

morphology.note: No images; pathway and disorders shown as schematic cards.

verification.notes: 5 factual claims checked (Huang 2022, Guerra Ruiz 2021, Newsome 2018, Morais 2022, Bhutani 2013, Zhang 2021, Lindqvist 2025 read in full text; Sofronescu 2012 and Ihara 1992 read as abstracts only); 1 claim pending (reviewer figures for hemolysis, Gilbert ceiling, choledocholithiasis and the 20 mg/dL deposition figure). The 2022 AAP guideline was not read (not open access). No human expert has reviewed this lesson.
